text: I still remember the first time I stepped onto campus as a freshman. Everything felt enormous: the buildings, the crowds, and especially the sense that I had no idea what I was doing. During those first few weeks, I struggled to find my place. I joined a few clubs, but I often felt like an outsider looking in. Things began to change when I started volunteering at a local tutoring center. Working with middle school students reminded me why I had chosen to study education in the first place. Their curiosity was contagious, and their small victories felt like my own. Over time, I realized that belonging is not something you find; it is something you build through consistent effort and genuine connection. Looking back, those uncertain early days taught me resilience, and I am grateful for every moment of them.
